content: My coffee maker and I have an understanding. It works the night shift, I take the credit, and neither of us talks about the decaf incident.
Somebody told me the older you get, the wiser you become. So far I have mostly become better at finding my glasses on top of my head.
Church potlucks are proof that God loves variety. Seven green bean casseroles, and not one of them tastes the same.
My dog thinks I leave every night to go save the world. I have not had the heart to tell him I just sit in a chair and play hymns.
Ever notice how the coffee always smells better than it tastes at this hour? That is the Lord teaching us humility, one mug at a time.
A friend asked if I ever get sleepy on the overnight. Only between songs, during songs, and right about now.
They say laughter is good medicine. If that is true, my family reunions should be covered by insurance.
One time I ordered a fancy coffee drink. It had more syllables than my last three prayers combined, and I went right back to plain black.
Truckers, if you see a fellow waving at you on the highway tonight, that is probably just me in spirit. I would wave harder, but I am holding coffee.
My grandmother could quote the entire book of Psalms and still not remember where she put her purse. I am beginning to understand her.
The choir director at my old church said I had a voice that could fill a room. Then she politely suggested I fill a different room.
Nothing tests your sanctification like a church parking lot after the Easter service.
I keep a list of things I want to remember. I just wish I could remember where I put the list.
The cat walked across my keyboard earlier and typed a perfect line of gibberish. Honestly, it read better than some of my first drafts.
Getting older means your back goes out more often than you do.
To all the new parents awake right now, that tiny person will one day sleep until noon. Hold on to that promise. It is not in Scripture, but it is true.
Years ago I fell asleep during a sermon on staying alert. The pastor said it was the best illustration he ever had.
My doctor told me to cut back on caffeine. I said, doctor, I host an overnight radio show. He said, never mind.
People ask me what my favorite hymn is. That is like asking which grandchild you love most. The answer depends on who is listening.
At my age I hum hymns without noticing, and the grocery store clerk now knows all four verses of Blessed Assurance.
The best part of the overnight shift is the commute. No traffic, no hurry, and the moon is always on time.
My wife says I snore in four part harmony. I like to think of it as a ministry.
If you ever doubt that God has a sense of humor, just look at a giraffe. Or a platypus. Or me before my first cup of coffee.
Noah ran the first floating zoo, and I bet he never once complained about the night shift. Then again, he had the animals to keep him up.
We bought one of those smart speakers. It understands everybody in the house except me. I think it has a problem with authority.
My knees have started making announcements before I stand up. Nobody asked them to, but they are very faithful about it.
Old hymnals had those little shape notes. I never learned to read them, but I could tell you which pages had the best doodles in the margins.
Ever try to sneak into the house late at night? The floor finds every squeak, and the dog announces you like a herald angel.
I was going to tell you a joke about the church organ, but it has too many stops.
Somebody said I have a face made for radio. I took it as a compliment, and so should you.
The Bible says to make a joyful noise. It does not say it has to be on key, and for that I am deeply grateful.
My grandson asked me what it was like before the internet. I told him we had to wait a whole week to forget what we were arguing about.
Insomniacs, welcome. We are the only club where the meetings start when everybody else goes home.
Last spring I took up walking for my health. So far my health is fine, but my shoes are worn out.
Every family has that one relative who says grace for twenty minutes while the gravy gets cold. In mine, that relative is me.
You know you are getting older when your favorite part of the day is finding a good parking spot.
There is nothing quite like a fellowship hall coffee urn. It holds forty cups and tastes like it has been holding them since nineteen seventy two.
My pastor says patience is a virtue. My microwave disagrees. Ninety seconds feels like an eternity at this hour.
Yoga and I tried to be friends once. The instructor said find your center. I found the floor, and I stayed there a while.
Moses got the commandments on stone tablets. I got my grocery list on the back of an envelope, and somehow mine still got lost.
My dog sits with me while I listen to the Gaither Trio. I am not saying he sings along, but his tail keeps perfect time.
They say you can not teach an old dog new tricks. I am an old dog who just learned how to make a video call, so there.
Somebody told me sleep is for the weak. Well, I would like to be weak for about eight hours, please and thank you.
The older I get, the more I relate to the song I Shall Not Be Moved. Mostly because getting out of this chair takes three tries.
At my house the remote control has a ministry of its own. It disappears, we pray, and it returns. Every single time.
Overnight radio is a funny thing. I talk to thousands of people and never once have to make eye contact. It suits me fine.
Mother used to say cleanliness is next to godliness. My teenage bedroom was apparently in a different county.
If you are driving a big rig right now, you are basically a night owl with eighteen wheels. I salute you from my much smaller chair.
A little boy once asked me if I was older than the Bible. I told him no, but I did own one of the first hymnals with pictures.
Have you noticed that the snooze button is the most used and least helpful invention in history?
There is a coffee mug on my desk that says World's Okayest Disc Jockey. My family gave it to me. I am choosing to believe it was affectionate.
Church softball league taught me two things. Forgiveness is necessary, and I should never be allowed near third base.
Do I talk to myself during the long overnight hours? Only when I need expert advice.
Grandkids are God's way of saying, you thought you were tired before?
Once I tried to diet. Then someone brought a pound cake to Bible study, and I decided I was called to a different ministry.
My reading glasses need their own reading glasses now. That is how you know you have been around a while.
Up this late? Me too. Let us agree not to tell anyone how many cookies we have eaten tonight.
Why is it that the hymn with the most verses is always the one where the song leader says, let us sing them all?
My cat believes the Sabbath is every day. She has never worked a shift in her life, and she seems perfectly at peace with it.
In my younger days I could stay up all night. Now I stay up all night and they pay me for it, which is about the only thing that got better.
The good news is, coffee is a gift from God. The bad news is, I have been unwrapping it all night.
Fixing a leaky faucet myself seemed like a good idea. Now we have a fountain. My wife calls it a water feature to make me feel better.
A teenager asked me what a cassette tape was. I said, imagine a playlist that eats itself if you look at it wrong.
Grandpa said the secret to a long marriage was two words. Yes, dear. He was married sixty one years, so I am inclined to believe him.
Some folks count sheep to fall asleep. I count the hymns I know by heart, and I usually drift off right around number two hundred.
Is it just me, or does the refrigerator light seem brighter after midnight? It is practically a lighthouse.
My first car had a radio with two stations, and one of them was mostly static. Look at us now.
People tell me I give great advice. They also tell me I never take it. Both are true.
The church van I learned to drive in had a door that only opened if you said a prayer and kicked it at the same time. Faith and works.
Ever pray for patience and then immediately get stuck behind a tractor? The Lord answers fast sometimes.
Somebody tell my body clock that I work nights. It keeps waking me at six in the morning like it has somewhere to be.
I asked my wife if she thought I was getting forgetful. She said I asked her that yesterday.
Our church bulletin once had a typo announcing the bake sale as the fake sale. Best attendance we ever had.
Not once has my dog read a book on contentment, yet he is the most content creature I know. A warm spot and a pat on the head does it.
Night shift nurses, you deserve a medal. Or at least a hot cup of coffee that nobody interrupts. I am praying for the coffee.
Counting my blessings tonight went fine until the third cup of coffee. Then I was counting faster than I could keep up.
When I was young, I thought forty was old. Now I think forty is when you just start figuring out where the light switches are.
My hearing is fine, I promise. I just prefer to listen with my whole heart, which is why I keep saying pardon.
Hymn writers in the old days wrote seven verses because they had no television. I respect the commitment.
You can tell a lot about a church by its coffee. Strong coffee usually means somebody in that kitchen loves you.
My granddaughter told me my phone is a dinosaur. I told her so am I, and we both still work.
How do I stay awake all night? Three things. Prayer, good music, and a chair that is just uncomfortable enough.
I am at the age where a nap is not a luxury. It is a scheduled appointment, and I never miss it.
Hear a squeak in the background? Relax, that is not the equipment. That is my chair reminding me about the cookies.
The neighbor's rooster crows at three in the morning. I think he is just trying to get on the radio.
Little kids pray the most honest prayers. I once heard one ask God to bless Mommy, Daddy, and the ice cream truck. Amen to that.
My wife labels everything in our pantry. I once found a jar labeled mystery. I ate it anyway. Faith is a powerful thing.
Some people have bucket lists. At my age I have a nap list, and I am working through it steadily.
Whistling along with a Rick Foster song seemed like a fine idea. My dog left the room. Everybody is a critic.
Ever notice how quiet the world gets around three in the morning? It is like everyone agreed to let us have the place to ourselves.
I am told I tell the same stories over and over. I like to think of them as classics in heavy rotation.
A man at church asked me if I was the voice on the radio. I said yes, and he said, huh, I pictured you taller. Me too, friend. Me too.
Grandmother made pies so good they should have been counted as a spiritual gift.
That step counter I bought was supposed to make me healthier. Mostly it tells me how many times I walk to the kitchen.
Remember when phones were attached to the wall? You could not lose them, and you could not take them to the dinner table. Simpler times.
My wife says I am a hopeless romantic. I say I am a hopeful one. There is a difference, and it usually involves flowers.
Am I a morning person? I am a whatever time it is person, as long as there is coffee.
Parents of toddlers, if your little one is up right now, the King's Heralds are here to help. They are much better singers than I am.
Sat on my glasses again tonight. That makes three pairs this year. The optometrist sends me a Christmas card.
Every church has a fellow who has brought the same casserole to every potluck since nineteen eighty. We love him, and we love that casserole.
My first sermon as a young man lasted six minutes. The deacons called it the best sermon they ever heard. I am still not sure that was a compliment.
Never trust a dog to watch your plate. I learned that the hard way at a church picnic, and the dog learned to love potato salad.
Back before I did this for a living, I tried to stay up for the sunrise and fell asleep at four. Now the sunrise and I are on a first name basis.
Here is my advice for the night. If the cookie jar is calling your name, at least make it say please.
My mechanic says my car has character. I think that means it makes noises he can not explain either.
The old church hymnals were so heavy you could do arm curls during the invitation hymn. Sixteen verses of Just As I Am and you were in great shape.
My grandson says I should get on social media. I told him I already have a following. It is called the overnight audience, and you are wonderful.
What do I do when I can not sleep? Simple. I go to work and talk to all of you.
Ever looked for your keys for ten minutes while holding them in your hand? Asking for a friend. Me. I am the friend.
I have a tie for every season of the church year. My wife says I have a tie for every season of the decade, mostly the seventies.
Somewhere tonight a sunrise is already on its way. It does not need your help to arrive, and neither does God's mercy.
The stars over your house right now were named by the same God who knows your name. That is worth thinking about on the drive home.
Every great hymn started as one person sitting quietly with God and a blank page. Your quiet hour could be the beginning of something too.
Faith is not the absence of questions. It is choosing to walk with God while the questions are still being answered.
Grace has a way of showing up before we even think to ask for it. Like a porch light left on for a traveler.
The old saints who wrote these hymns knew hard times. They wrote about joy anyway, and that is the testimony.
A single candle does not argue with the darkness. It simply shines. Be that kind of light tomorrow.
Jesus spent whole nights in prayer. If you are awake right now, you are in very good company.
God does some of His finest work in the dark. Seeds sprout underground, and dawn comes after midnight.
Kindness is a quiet sermon. Most people will never hear you preach, but they will remember how you treated them.
The same hands that flung the stars into space were pierced for you. Let that kind of love make you brave.
Small faithfulness adds up. A prayer here, a kind word there, and one day you look back and see a whole cathedral.
When the world gets loud, heaven often whispers. The overnight hours are a good time to listen.
You may never know whose life your faith is shaping. Someone is watching how you trust God, and it is helping them believe.
Every morning God hands us a clean page. What we write on it matters, but His mercy covers the smudges.
Love that costs nothing is easy to find. Love that costs everything was found at the cross.
Hope is not wishful thinking. For the Christian, it is confident expectation rooted in a God who keeps His word.
Think of the people who prayed for you before you ever knew it. Tonight might be the night you pay that forward.
The hymn writers did not have fancy studios. They had pencils, paper, and a God worth singing about. That was enough.
Your life is a letter that God is writing to the world. Some chapters are hard to read, but He knows how the story ends.
Courage is not feeling fearless. It is taking the next faithful step while your knees are still shaking.
A tree does not grow strong in calm weather alone. The wind teaches the roots to hold on.
Forgiveness is a gift you give that comes back to bless your own heart. A grudge is a heavy thing to carry through the night.
Some of the strongest people I know never made headlines. They just showed up, prayed hard, and loved well for fifty years.
The empty tomb means the last word never belongs to death. It belongs to Jesus, and His word is life.
Gratitude turns what we have into enough. Try naming three good gifts from today before the next song ends.
Every act of service is worship when it is done for Jesus. Even the dishes. Even the double shift.
God is not in a hurry, but He is never late. The timing of heaven is perfect, even when it feels slow down here.
Prayer is not a last resort. It is the first and best conversation of the day, or the night.
The moon has no light of its own. It only reflects the sun. That is a pretty good picture of what we are called to do.
Great faith often starts as small obedience. Do the next right thing, and leave the big picture to God.
The church is not a building. It is a family scattered across the night, and some of them are listening right now.
Humility is not thinking less of yourself. It is thinking of yourself less, and of others more.
Heaven keeps no record of how impressive we were. It celebrates how faithful we were.
The gospel is the best news ever told. A Savior came looking for us when we were not looking for Him.
One person who keeps praying can change the spiritual weather of a whole family.
Joy and sorrow can sit at the same table. The Christian life makes room for both, with Jesus at the head.
A gentle answer can calm a storm better than the loudest argument. Try it tomorrow and watch what happens.
These songs were written by people who knew that tomorrow was not promised, but eternity was.
The light from some stars left them thousands of years ago. God's promises are even older, and they still shine.
When you can not see the way, remember the One who is the Way.
Integrity is what you do when nobody is watching. At this hour, that is most of us. God sees, and He delights in faithfulness.
Encouragement is like oxygen. Most people do not notice how much they need it until someone gives them a little.
A grateful heart is a magnet for joy. Not because life is easy, but because God is good.
Jesus washed feet. If the King of glory could kneel, none of us are too important to serve.
Our work does not have to be famous to be holy. The farmer, the nurse, and the trucker all reflect the Creator.
Some prayers are answered with yes, some with wait, and some with something better. All of them are heard.
Generations of believers have sung these same words in the dark. Their faith became our inheritance.
Peace is not the absence of trouble. It is the presence of Jesus in the middle of it.
Tomorrow you will meet someone who needs a kind word. Start practicing tonight.
The cross turned the worst day in history into the doorway of hope. God can redeem your hard days too.
A life well lived is not measured in years but in love given away.
There is a reason the old hymns last. Truth does not go out of style.
God wastes nothing. Not the tears, not the waiting, not the long nights. He weaves it all together.
Faith grows best when it is used. Like a muscle, it gets stronger every time you lean on God.
Picture every believer awake right now, scattered across the map, all looking toward the same Savior. That is a beautiful thought.
The Lord can make a highway in the wilderness. That includes the stretch of road some of you are driving tonight.
Mercy is not getting what we deserve. Grace is getting what we never could have earned. God gives us both, every day.
Simple acts of love never go out of season. A casserole, a card, a phone call. These things matter in the kingdom.
If God can paint a sunset fresh every evening, He can surely make something new in you.
The quiet faithfulness of grandparents has shaped more lives than most sermons ever will.
Hope is a song you sing before you see the sunrise. Keep singing, friend.
Every heartbeat is an invitation to trust God a little more. You have had quite a few of them today.
Christ did not come merely to make bad people better. He came to make dead hearts alive. That is the wonder of grace.
Worship is not just singing. It is a life laid down, a heart lifted up, and a will surrendered.
The darkest hour of the night is still under the rule of the God who created light.
Faithfulness in small things prepares us for the big ones. God notices both.
Kindness is a language everyone understands, even the folks who have never opened a Bible.
Somewhere a believer is praying for people they have never met. Maybe tonight that includes you.
A legacy is not what you leave for people. It is what you leave in them.
The love of God is not a reward for good behavior. It is the starting point for everything.
Even the smallest lamp can guide a lost traveler home. Your faith does not need to be big to help someone.
No pit is so deep that the love of God is not deeper still. Corrie ten Boom learned that in a very dark place, and she lived to tell it.
When we sing about heaven, we are not escaping life. We are remembering where it is all headed.
Rest is not laziness. Even God rested on the seventh day. Taking time to be still is an act of trust.
Every new believer is a reason for heaven to throw a party. The angels rejoice over one sinner who repents.
Your scars can become someone else's map to healing. God uses our stories when we let Him.
The greatest things in life are not things. They are people, and the God who made them.
Contentment is learning to say, Lord, this is enough, because You are here.
The first Christmas announcement went to shepherds on the night shift. God has always had a soft spot for the overnight crowd.
A soft heart in a hard world is not weakness. It is a mark of the Spirit's work.
The resurrection is not just a doctrine. It is a promise with your name on it.
Let your faith be like the old oak tree. Not flashy, just deeply rooted and still standing after many storms.
Love your neighbor might mean the one next door, or the one in the next lane, or the one on the other end of the phone tonight.
Wisdom often comes wrapped in gray hair and patient eyes. Listen to the older saints when you can.
We do not have to understand everything to trust Someone who does.
Every Sunday the church gathers to remember that Jesus is risen. Even at midnight on a Tuesday, it is still true.
Obedience is a beautiful form of praise. Singing is good, but walking with God every day sings even louder.
Pray for the people on your street tonight, by name if you can. It is the quietest way to change a neighborhood.
Holiness is not a cage. It is the freedom to be who God made you to be.
Somewhere in the world it is morning, and believers are just waking up to praise. The song never stops.
Wherever you go, you are an ambassador of heaven, even at the truck stop or the hospital break room.
The best sermons are lived, not preached. Your quiet example speaks volumes.
God took a shepherd boy and made a king. He took fishermen and made apostles. Imagine what He can do with a willing heart.
Thankfulness is the soil where joy grows. Plant a little tonight.
Generosity is not about how much you have. The widow gave two small coins and Jesus said she gave more than all the rest.
Some of the most beautiful music comes from instruments that were broken and mended. People are like that too.
Grace does not just forgive us. It changes us, slowly and surely, into the likeness of Christ.
The night is a wonderful time to remember that God never sleeps. He is keeping watch over the whole world.
Every hymn we play tonight is a little seed of truth. You never know where it might take root.
A whispered prayer reaches heaven just as fast as a shouted one. Distance is never the problem with God.
The way of Jesus is often the slow way, the humble way, the loving way. It is also the only way that lasts.
Hospitality turns strangers into friends and friends into family. The early church was famous for it.
When we reach the end of ourselves, we find the beginning of God's strength.
If you are sitting in a hospital waiting room tonight, you are not waiting alone. The Lord is right there in the next chair.
Feeling worn thin? That is okay. God does not need you at full strength to love you fully.
To the caregiver who has not slept in days, your love is seen. Every quiet act of care is noticed in heaven.
Grief is love with nowhere to go. If you are missing someone tonight, bring that ache to Jesus. He wept too.
You do not have to have it all figured out by morning. Just make it through this next hour with God.
Truckers on a long haul tonight, may the Lord keep your eyes clear, your road safe, and your heart at peace.
Made a mess of today? Here is good news. His mercies are new every morning, and morning is coming.
Lonely tonight? This radio is a small reminder that many of us are awake together, and God is with each one.
New moms and dads rocking a little one in the dark, you are doing holy work, even if it does not feel like it at four in the morning.
You are not too far gone. There is no road so long that God can not walk it to bring you home.
If worry is sitting on your chest tonight, try telling God exactly what it is. He can carry what you can not.
Nurses, doctors, aides, and techs on shift right now, thank you. You are the hands of Christ to people in their hardest hours.
Sometimes the bravest thing you can do is get up tomorrow and try again. You can do that. God will help.
You matter. Not because of what you do, but because of whose you are.
The night feels long, but it is not forever. Joy comes in the morning, and that is a promise.
Feel like your prayers are hitting the ceiling? Keep praying. God hears through plaster and pain alike.
To anyone fighting a battle no one else sees, the Lord sees it. You are not invisible to Him.
Take a deep breath. Let it out slowly. You are still here, and God is still God.
Older saints listening tonight, your prayers are holding up more people than you know. Do not ever think your work is done.
When the house is quiet and the thoughts are loud, remember that the Shepherd still watches over His sheep.
Lost someone this year? The empty chair is real. So is the hope of reunion in Christ. Hold both.
Permission granted to rest, friend. God is not grading you on how tired you are.
That mistake does not define you. The cross does. And the cross says forgiven.
For the one working a job you do not love to provide for people you do, that is a beautiful kind of faithfulness.
If tonight feels heavy, let this next song hold some of the weight for a few minutes.
Every hard day so far, you have made it through, and God was with you for every one of them. He is not leaving now.
Feeling forgotten? God engraved you on the palms of His hands. You could not be more remembered.
Up with a sick child tonight? May the Lord give you strength and give that little one rest.
It is okay to not be okay. Just do not stay alone in it. Reach out to someone tomorrow. You are worth the call.
Small steps count. If all you did today was keep going, that is still going.
Whatever you are facing, you are facing it with the God who parted seas and calmed storms.
Shift workers eating dinner at three in the morning, enjoy every bite. You earned it.
Your story is not over. There are chapters ahead you can not imagine yet, and God is writing them with care.
Feel like a failure as a parent tonight? The very fact that you care so much says otherwise.
Doubt is not the opposite of faith. It is often the doorway to a deeper faith. Bring your questions to God.
Waiting on test results? Waiting on a phone call? God is not anxious about tomorrow. Let Him hold that for you.
Nobody has to earn a place at God's table. Jesus already pulled out the chair for you.
When you can not pray, the Spirit prays for you with groanings too deep for words. You are covered.
Driving home tired? Pull over if you need to. Your family wants you home more than they want you home early.
For the widow and the widower listening tonight, you are part of a family that will not forget you. Neither will God.
Some nights, survival is the victory. Tonight might be one of those, and that is enough.
Remember that the Lord is close to the brokenhearted. Closer than the dark, closer than your fears.
Has someone hurt you? Your pain is real and it matters to God. He is a God of justice and of healing.
Hold on, friend. The tide turns, the seasons change, and God remains faithful through all of it.
Nobody needs you to be strong for everyone tonight. Let God be strong for you.
Far from home tonight? The same God who watches over your loved ones is watching over you.
Students up late studying, God gave you that mind. Use it well, and do not forget to sleep eventually.
Your tears are not wasted. Scripture says God keeps them in a bottle. Every one is precious to Him.
If addiction is fighting you tonight, there is hope and there is help. One more hour clean is one more hour of victory.
A new day is coming whether you feel ready or not. And God will already be in it, waiting for you.
For those caring for parents who once cared for them, what a full circle of love. God honors that sacrifice.
Nobody is behind in life. You are right where God can meet you, and He is good at meeting people right where they are.
Is your marriage struggling tonight? Do not give up on the God who specializes in restoration.
Rest your mind on this. Nothing that worries you tonight has ever surprised God.
Feeling unqualified? God has a long history of using people who felt exactly the same way.
The prodigal's father ran to him. If you are thinking of coming home to God, He is already running toward you.
To the person in a quiet apartment tonight, you are seen, you are loved, and you are not alone on these airwaves.
When life feels like a storm, remember Jesus slept in the boat. Not because He did not care, but because He was in control.
A bruised reed He will not break. If you feel fragile tonight, you are in the gentlest hands there are.
Your worth was settled at Calvary. Nobody's opinion can lower that price.
Battling depression? Please hear this. You are worth fighting for, and people want to help. Talk to someone you trust.
Did today go sideways? Tomorrow is a fresh start, and God has never once run out of fresh starts.
Keep going. Somebody is going to need the strength you are building right now.
Maybe you feel like you are just getting by. Getting by with God is still walking with God.
Night watchmen, security guards, dispatchers on duty, thank you for keeping watch while the rest of us rest.
Burdens shared are lighter. Is there a friend you could call tomorrow and let in a little?
Been carrying shame? Set it down. Jesus took it to the cross so you would not have to carry it anymore.
Your season of waiting is not a season of wasting. God is working, even when nothing seems to move.
Hurting people are often the most compassionate people. God may be growing that gift in you right now.
Child of the King, that is you, even in your pajamas at four in the morning. Royalty has never looked so comfortable.
Faith feeling weak? Remember, a mustard seed is pretty small, and Jesus said that was plenty.
The Lord will fight for you. Sometimes your only job is to be still and let Him.
Just got hard news? Then take it one hour at a time. You do not have to solve tomorrow tonight.
Fear knocked at the door. Faith answered. And no one was there. That old saying still holds up beautifully.
When you feel like you have nothing left to give, receive instead. God loves to fill empty cups.
More people are in your corner than you realize, including the One who created the stars.
For folks recovering from surgery or illness, healing takes time. Be patient with your body and kind to yourself.
Lying awake replaying the day? Hand the tape over to God. He can edit what you can not.
Not every chapter is a happy one, but every chapter is held by the Author. Turn the page with Him.
Your prayers for your prodigal are not wasted. Keep praying. God loves that child even more than you do.
The enemy says you are finished. God says you are forgiven, and you are just getting started.
Feeling invisible at work? God sees the extra effort, the integrity, and the late hours. You serve an audience of One.
Nobody can pour from an empty cup. Take time to be filled by prayer, Scripture, and a little sleep when you can.
Weeping may last for the night, but this is not the end of the story.
On the road tonight away from family? May God bless the miles and bring you home safely.
God's love for you is not fragile. You can not break it, and you can not wear it out.
Even a bad day has a sunset, and every sunset has a sunrise behind it.
When others leave, Jesus stays. He promised never to leave you or forsake you.
Struggling to forgive yourself? If God has forgiven you, who are you to overrule Him? Let it go, friend.
Single parents juggling it all tonight, God sees your sacrifice, and He is never too busy for you.
Need strength for tomorrow? Ask for it tomorrow. Tonight, ask for rest. God's provision comes one day at a time.
Hear me on this. You are not your diagnosis, your bank balance, or your past. You are beloved.
Let today's worries end with today. Tomorrow has enough of its own, and God already has it covered.
A broken heart is not the end of love. Often it is where God's love gets in deepest.
Whoever needs to hear it tonight, you are doing better than you think.
In every valley, the Shepherd walks ahead. Follow Him through, one step at a time.
Just lost a pet? Your grief makes sense. Love is love, and God cares about what breaks your heart.
Do not compare your behind the scenes to everyone else's highlight reel. God is not grading on that curve.
